fragments.text: V8 snapshots save 81% require() time in Electron but cannot snapshot native addons (better-sqlite3), process/stdout-touching modules (Ink), or network modules (MCP SDK)
Unreal Engine LOD: load lightweight stub first, swap to full asset when player approaches. Node.js: Proxy-based module stub that replaces itself on first method call
id Software virtual textures: page table maps export names to byte ranges in concatenated bundle. Only the called export's bytes are read from disk
UE5 World Partition: pre-compute minimum dependency subgraph per CLI command at build time. Only bootstrap the intersection of all commands (~5MB core)

Bacillus subtilis spore germination: Stage I structural restore in seconds (Ca-DPA release, SASP degradation), Stage II slow metabolic resume. Software: render TUI frame in Stage I, load agent in Stage II
Tardigrade anhydrobiosis: replace water with trehalose glass matrix, lose 97% volume, restore on rehydration. Software: serialize config to frozen JSON blob at exit, JSON.parse (<1ms) to restore
ESP32 three-stage boot: ROM bootloader → second-stage from flash → full app with FreeRTOS. Each stage only loads what the next needs. Stage N has zero imports from stage N+2
Embedded hot/cold module partitioning: linker places .text in flash (XIP), .data in RAM. Hot code in fast SRAM. Build-time lint enforces the boundary
Chrome zygote pattern: fork pre-initialized process before threads start. COW shares ~8MB library state. Constraint: must fork before libuv thread pool starts, macOS Mach port issues
Daemon + Unix socket: 130μs round-trip. PM2 uses this pattern. Eliminates cold start entirely but makes memory permanent (worse for 'reduce memory' goal)
Bun memory data is contradictory: Trigger.dev reports -55%, but production reports show +75% for long-running processes. Ink on Bun is untested. No reliable step-function improvement

CRITICAL: PrefixFingerprint depends on toolsSha256 from ToolRegistry. If PromptEngine or ToolRegistry are deferred to Stage 2, first API call gets wrong hash → prefix cache miss. This is Rivet's core competitive advantage

App.tsx is a 40+ import monolith coupling TUI and agent. There is no 'shell-only' boundary. React.lazy/Suspense not documented for Ink. Cannot split Stage 1 TUI from Stage 2 agent without major refactoring
AgentLoop constructor eagerly instantiates 15+ subsystems with side effects (file I/O, filesystem watches). Proxy stubs cannot defer constructors, only method calls
V2 (dual process) extinct: worker_threads don't share V8 heap, each has ~40MB baseline. Two processes = 140MB, worse than single process 135MB
V3 (daemon) extinct: contradicts user's core concern 'memory usage'. 135MB permanent resident is worse than 135MB transient
Convergence insight: Rivet's startup memory problem is not 'too many modules' but 'loaded too early'. The fix is identifying 'when is it actually needed' and deferring to that moment
